claim: On November 18, 2026 Fitbit's token endpoint answered HTTP 410 Gone with a message that the legacy endpoints were decommissioned on October 30, 2026 (read through source-snapshot run 44408817217, logs deleted).
quote: The legacy Fitbit Web API and OAuth 2.0 endpoints were decommissioned on October 30, 2026.

claim: Google's Google Health API page gives November 2, 2026 as the turn-off, in the past tense (read 2026-11-21).
quote: November 2, 2026 (API turn-off): The Fitbit Web API and Fitbit OAuth endpoints were turned off and no longer function or sync data to or from Google Health users.

claim: Google's Google Health help article says Fitbit connections retired on October 30, 2026 (read 2026-11-18).
quote: Google Health Support can’t restore or fix your broken connection once Fitbit connections retired on October 30, 2026.

claim: Rate limit: 150 API requests per hour per consented user, resetting approximately at the top of each hour.
quote: An application’s rate limit is 150 API requests per hour for each user who has consented to share their data; and it resets, approximately, at the top of each hour.

claim: Each re-consent counts toward the Google Cloud project's OAuth token grant rate limit; more than 10,000 in a 24-hour window needs a higher quota requested in advance.
quote: If you expect to exceed 10,000 user sign-ups or re-authentications within a 24-hour sliding window during your migration

claim: The rate-limit headers, including Fitbit-Rate-Limit-Reset, the seconds until the reset.
quote: Fitbit-Rate-Limit-Reset : The number of seconds until the rate limit resets.

claim: A Google account registered as a Fitbit developer account is required.
quote: To use the Fitbit APIs, you need to have a Google account registered as a Fitbit developer account.

claim: Google Workspace accounts are not supported.
quote: Google Workspace accounts are not supported with Fitbit.

claim: The code verifier is a cryptographically random value of 43 to 128 characters.
quote: A cryptographically random value between 43-128 characters long called a code verifier

claim: Only server apps may omit PKCE.
quote: Only server application types may omit PKCE.

claim: An app may not force a user to grant every scope.
quote: The application is not allowed to enable all scopes by default or force a user to enable all scopes.

claim: Fitbit's example token response shows expires_in of 28800 seconds.
